items.title: Figma July release notes: auto layout now aligns with CSS to cut design-to-code handoff friction
items.excerpt: Figma's July 24 release-notes entry, 'Design closer to CSS with the updated auto layout option,' reworks auto layout so its behavior matches how CSS handles layout, reducing the developer workarounds needed at handoff. It lands in a July run that also bound code-backed screens to existing file variables (July 16) and shipped GPT-5.6 inside Figma Make (July 9) — incremental but real changes tightening the design-to-code loop that AI-assisted workflows now depend on.

items.title: DESIGN.md: the '.cursorrules for your design system' that stops AI UI style drift
items.excerpt: The piece proposes DESIGN.md as a portable, structured file that stops AI coding agents from 'guessing' a design system and drifting on colors, spacing, and component behavior across sessions. It uses a dual layer — machine-readable YAML front matter for exact design tokens plus human-readable Markdown for the intent behind them — so agents build UI against a durable source of truth, positioned as the design-system analogue to a .cursorrules file. A concrete answer to visual-identity drift, the biggest consistency failure in agentic UI generation.

items.title: Character consistency across 24 pages of an AI-generated picture book
items.excerpt: A hands-on breakdown of keeping a character recognizably the same across a full 24-page generated picture book, separating identity consistency (the same child) from style consistency (a uniform illustration aesthetic) as distinct problems. Techniques include fixing all generation parameters (model version, sampler, step count, style tokens), regenerating whole books rather than single pages, weighting identity conditioning heavily, and evaluating at the set level with pairwise face-embedding distance and palette comparison. A craft-level look at production generative-image workflows for designers and illustrators.

items.title: Vibe coding won't kill developers — it'll kill the middle
items.excerpt: The essay argues AI-assisted 'vibe coding' won't eliminate builders as a class but will liquify the middle tier — the implementation work done against known specs — much as cheap cameras spared top photographers while gutting commodity work. Value concentrates in roles requiring architectural judgment, domain expertise, taste, and strategy. A sharp framing of the AX skills shift facing designers-who-build and design engineers as prompt-to-app tools commoditize execution.

items.title: Google thinks maths proves its AI is genuinely creative — but is it?
items.excerpt: Creative Bloq interrogates Google's claim — resting on AI systems solving and generating novel mathematics — that its models are 'genuinely creative,' weighing what mathematical novelty does and doesn't prove about creativity for artists and designers. The framing matters for creatives because 'is the machine creative?' underpins how much of ideation and concepting teams are willing to hand to generative tools.

items.title: Hate generative AI? Maybe it's time to boycott Netflix
items.excerpt: With Netflix leaning into generative AI across its productions, Creative Bloq argues creatives angry about AI's encroachment on craft should vote with their subscriptions. It's a look at how a major studio's gen-AI adoption reshapes creative and design work and the leverage audiences and practitioners still hold — a culture-and-craft read on the design/creative industry's AI backlash.
